# Table of Contents {.unnumbered .unlisted}

```{=latex}
% Using \@starttoc{toc} instead of \tableofcontents: the latter
% would print its own internal \chapter*{Contents} heading on top
% of the Markdown heading above, producing a second, blank
% chapter-opening page. \@starttoc{toc} just dumps the entries.
\makeatletter
\@starttoc{toc}
\makeatother
```

```{=latex}
% List of Tables and List of Figures, in raw LaTeX rather than
% Markdown headings — \giOptionalTOCList (defined in preamble.tex)
% checks whether each one actually has any entries first, and prints
% nothing at all (no heading, no page) if not. See preamble.tex's
% "OPTIONAL LIST OF TABLES / LIST OF FIGURES" section for the full
% explanation of why this can't be done with a Markdown heading.
\giOptionalTOCList{lot}{List of Tables}
\giOptionalTOCList{lof}{List of Figures}
```

```{=latex}
\giMarkFrontMatterEnd
\giEnableMainMatter
```
